item.title: Sancionada, lei do seguro rural no Brasil traz previsibilidade sobre recursos
item.description: O novo marco regulatório do seguro rural do Brasil traz mais previsibilidade para o setor agrícola, afirmaram nesta quarta-feira entidades de classe, apontando que as mudanças devem colaborar para evitar contingenciamentos de recursos que afetaram a contratação do mecanismo de proteção de renda dos agricultores nos últimos anos.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O novo marco regulatório do seguro rural do Brasil traz mais previsibilidade para o setor agrícola, afirmaram nesta quarta-feira entidades de classe, apontando que as mudanças devem colaborar para evitar contingenciamentos de recursos que afetaram a contratação do mecanismo de proteção de renda dos agricultores nos últimos anos. A sanção pelo presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva à lei originária em projeto de autoria da senadora Tereza Cristina (PP), ex-ministra da Agricultura no governo de Jair Bolsonaro, estabelece que a subvenção governamental ao prêmio do seguro rural terá caráter obrigatório, limitada ao montante previsto no Projeto de Lei Orçamentária Anual (Ploa) e condicionada à adoção de medidas de compensação. "Essa medida impede que as despesas relacionadas à subvenção sejam objeto de limitação de empenho e movimentação financeira", afirmou a associação de produtores Aprosoja Brasil, em nota. "Ainda que os limites previstos na legislação orçamentária e as medidas de compensação aplicáveis devam ser observados, a mudança de 'despesa discricionária' para 'despesa obrigatória" garante a execução da cifra destinada ao programa", acrescentou. No ano passado, por exemplo, de um orçamento público para o prêmio do seguro rural inicialmente previsto em R$1,06 bilhão, aproximadamente R$355 milhões foram cortados e R$90 milhões contingenciados, diante da instabilidade de recursos do governo, segundo avaliação da Confederação Nacional das Seguradoras (CNseg), da Associação Brasileira do Agronegócio (Abag) e da Associação Nacional das Instituições de Crédito, Financiamento e Investimento (Acrefi). Diante de recursos insuficientes para a subvenção ao prêmio, a parcela da área cultivada protegida contra intempéries caiu de 16,3% em 2021 para 3,3% em 2025, acrescentaram as entidades. A Aprosoja Brasil comentou ainda que o novo marco amplia e moderniza a estrutura do Fundo de Cobertura Suplementar dos Riscos do Seguro Rural, permitindo a participação de seguradoras, resseguradoras, empresas da cadeia produtiva do agronegócio e cooperativas de produção agropecuária. "Quanto maior o número de participantes dos fundos, maior é o compartilhamento de risco e o apoio disponível às próprias seguradoras", disse. A Confederação da Agricultura e Pecuária do Brasil (CNA) observou que a lei cria condições para a regulamentação desse Fundo de Catástrofe, que deverá funcionar como um "colchão de amortecimento para as seguradoras que estão em regiões críticas, onde há eventos climáticos extremos". Mas o diretor técnico da CNA, Bruno Lucchi, observou que o governo vetou o item que tratava de uma alternativa de fontes de recursos para o fundo, por meio das Letras de Risco de Seguro. O outro veto está relacionado à isenção de tributação do seguro. "Defendíamos essa isenção para ter preços de seguro ao produtor mais baixos. É um ponto que vamos discutir com a FPA (Frente Parlamentar da Agropecuária), sobre a possível derrubada do veto ligado à tributação do seguro", afirmou ele, em nota. Lucchi acrescentou que o próximo passo é aguardar a regulamentação da lei, que vai depender de decretos, de resoluções do Conselho Monetário Nacional (CMN) e da criação do Estatuto do Fundo. Essas questões, disse ele, "podem ter avanços em um futuro breve". O Sistema OCB (Organização das Cooperativas Brasileiras) destacou em nota que defendia a sanção integral do texto aprovado pelo Congresso Nacional, mas considera que os vetos não alteram esses pontos centrais da lei. A execução obrigatória do programa de subvenção ao prêmio do seguro precisa de uma medida de compensação orçamentária, procedimento usual quando uma lei altera a estrutura de despesas da União, explicou a organização. "O Sistema OCB espera que essa medida e a regulamentação da lei, que envolve decretos, resoluções e o estatuto do Fundo Catástrofe, sejam concluídas nos próximos meses, para que as novas regras alcancem os produtores nas próximas safras", disse. As entidades defendem que a previsibilidade do seguro rural é condição para perenidade no campo e planejamento para as safras no curto, médio e longo prazos. Outros avanços da nova legislação são a definição de prazos para regulação e liquidação de sinistros e o reconhecimento do seguro rural como garantia nas operações de crédito rural, apontou a Sociedade Rural Brasileira (SRB). O ministro da Agricultura, André de Paula, disse que a nova lei aproxima "o seguro do crédito", criando um mecanismo de garantia. Além disso, ele citou a previsibilidade de o setor não ver contingenciados recursos.

item.title: Steel forum calls for more tariffs, fewer subsidies to fight excess capacity
item.description: Members of an OECD forum on excess steel capacity agreed on Wednesday to work towards imposing more tariffs on steel from China and other overproducing countries, and to refrain from subsidies that maintain loss-making steel mills or encourage new uneconomic plants.
item.dc:creator: David Lawder
item.content:encoded: Members of an OECD forum on excess steel capacity agreed on Wednesday to work towards imposing more tariffs on steel from China and other overproducing countries, and to refrain from subsidies that maintain loss-making steel mills or encourage new uneconomic plants. The Global Forum on Steel Excess Capacity said in a statement that its membership of 28 market-oriented economies agreed on the new framework to combat excess production, as a US-led G20 trade ministers' meeting got underway in Milwaukee. The OECD said excess steel capacity above global demand is expected to increase to 745 million metric tons from 601 million tons in 2025. G20 member China, which produces over half the world's steel, is widely viewed as the largest source of excess capacity but is not a member of the forum, nor is India, the second-largest producer and a major exporter. US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer on Wednesday dubbed the agreement the "Milwaukee Framework," saying it would likely encourage countries to raise trade barriers to "hold accountable" countries such as China that are responsible for a flood of cheap steel. "Every country will do what they think is appropriate," Greer said of the agreement. "The United States has taken robust measures, and it probably makes sense for other countries to do that too." The forum agreed that member countries should open more anti-dumping, anti-subsidy and global safeguard investigations that could lead to new duties to protect domestic producers. It said countries should also apply other trade measures on imports of steel and "derivative products containing steel from sources of global excess capacity." The forum also agreed that countries should share more data on steel imports, including the "country of melt and pour" of the metal to help address circumvention of existing tariffs. Philip Bell, president of the Steel Manufacturers Association, said the framework is "a step in the right direction." Bell added in a statement that the Trump administration's tariffs on steel imports, now at 50% globally, "have created the stable, predictable market environment that domestic producers need to invest, expand, and compete" in the US. G20 FOCUS ON CHINA POLICIES China's excess industrial capacity and industrial subsidies have been key themes of the US-led G20 ministerial meetings so far this year. At a G20 finance ministers meeting in Asheville, North Carolina, earlier in September, [USN:L1N44T0JC TEXT:"all G20 member economies except China"] agreed to take action against "non-market" economic policies and trade distortions that cause over-reliance on exports. [USN:L6N44W0RE TEXT:"China's turbocharged exports"] have propped up its economic growth despite weak domestic demand, while flooding Europe, Latin America and other regions with cheap goods, pressuring domestic industries. Besides the steep tariffs on steel, the US has also banned imports of Chinese vehicles on national security data-collection grounds. Some foreign trade ministers present in Milwaukee were enthusiastic about the actions. "We see that China is really heavily subsidizing its production and export of steel products," said Andrzej Domanski, Poland's finance and economy minister. "This is a problem for many, many countries in the European Union, for Poland as well. And, of course, this is one of the issues that we want to raise here in the United States."

item.title: FDA seeks scientists and consumer representatives for advisory panels
item.description: The US Food and Drug Administration on Wednesday launched a nationwide effort to recruit scientists, medical experts and consumer representatives to its advisory committees, which advise the agency on drugs, vaccines and other regulated products.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The US Food and Drug Administration on Wednesday launched a nationwide effort to recruit scientists, medical experts and consumer representatives to its advisory committees, which advise the agency on drugs, vaccines and other regulated products. Here are few details: The agency is seeking candidates for current and expected vacancies in areas including oncology, cardiovascular medicine, neurology, genetics and medical devices, it said. FDA advisory committees, which include physicians, researchers, statisticians, patient advocates and consumer representatives, review scientific evidence and make independent recommendations to the agency. Their recommendations are not binding on the regulator. "We are actively inviting people from across the country who are on the forefront of their fields," acting FDA Commissioner Kyle Diamantas said. The FDA will accept nominations on a continuing basis, including self-nominations. It set a November 15 deadline for consumer representatives and November 30 for scientific and other voting members to receive first consideration for current and near-term vacancies. Members may serve terms of up to four years. The Department of Health and Human Services did not immediately respond to Reuters questions on how many positions are vacant or how the recruitment effort compares with previous drives.

item.title: US Justice Department files complaint against Minnesota judges who gave interviews about immigration surge
item.description: The US Justice Department filed a judicial misconduct complaint on Wednesday against judges in Minnesota who gave interviews to the New York Times about the immigration surge there, alleging it was unethical and partisan.
item.dc:creator: Dan Rosenzweig-Ziff, Andrew Goudsward
item.content:encoded: The US Justice Department filed a judicial misconduct complaint on Wednesday against judges in Minnesota who gave interviews to the New York Times about the immigration surge there, alleging it was unethical and partisan. In September, judges in Minnesota told the Times that the Trump administration had a "disregard for court orders" and its actions threatened the rule of law. Two did so on the record. The judicial misconduct complaint called the judges' conduct "particularly egregious." Misconduct complaints filed against other judges by the Justice Department under Trump have [USN:L1N3X00XW TEXT:"repeatedly been dismissed."] Attorney General Todd Blanche called the fact that the judges spoke to the media a "clear violation of their ethical duties" and criticized them for commenting on pending cases. He also asked the judges to recuse themselves from any case involving the Department of Homeland Security, alleging they had bias against the administration. It is unusual for sitting judges to comment on the record about cases, particularly those in the news. In February, though, [USN:L1N3Z81EI TEXT:"a judicial ethics panel released an opinion"] saying federal judges may advocate for greater security and defend colleagues against "illegitimate" attacks and criticism. They may also advocate for the rule of law and the independence of the judiciary, the ethics opinion said. Rebecca Parks, a spokesperson for the judges, cited that ethics opinion in a statement arguing the judges committed no wrongdoing. "As legal-ethics experts have confirmed, our judges were acting well within the ethical rules that apply to federal judges in speaking to the New York Times," she said, adding that they were advocating for the rule of law and judicial independence. The complaint was signed by the second- and third-ranking officials in the Department of Justice.

item.title: Retornos bonos Tesoro EEUU suben levemente; se reducen apuestas alza tasas Fed tras dato inflación
item.description: Los rendimientos de los bonos del Tesoro de Estados Unidos a más largo plazo subieron el miércoles, mientras que los a dos años se mantuvieron prácticamente sin cambios, a medida que los inversores asimilaban un aumento de la inflación en agosto menor al esperado y disminuían las apuestas sobre un alza de las tasas de interés por parte de la Reserva Federal en octubre.
item.dc:creator: Sinead Carew
item.content:encoded: Los rendimientos de los bonos del Tesoro de Estados Unidos a más largo plazo subieron el miércoles, mientras que los a dos años se mantuvieron prácticamente sin cambios, a medida que los inversores asimilaban un aumento de la inflación en agosto menor al esperado y disminuían las apuestas sobre un alza de las tasas de interés por parte de la Reserva Federal en octubre. * Antes de repuntar, los retornos a dos y 10 años habían ampliado inicialmente sus caídas después de que la Oficina de Análisis Económico (BEA) del Departamento de Comercio informara que el índice de precios de gastos de consumo personal (PCE) aumentó un 0,3 % el mes pasado, tras un incremento del 0,1% en julio, cifra revisada a la baja. * Los datos, publicados temprano el miércoles, mostraron que la inflación PCE subyacente aumentó un 3,0% interanual en agosto, tras un avance del 3,0% en julio, también revisado a la baja desde la estimación inicial del 3,3% para el periodo de 12 meses hasta julio. * En septiembre, los retornos de los bonos registraron su mayor avance mensual en años, ya que el conflicto en Oriente Medio ha mantenido elevados los precios del petróleo y ha generado dudas sobre cuándo se moderará una inflación que se resiste a ceder. * El mercado descontaba ahora una probabilidad de alrededor del 63% de que la Fed mantenga las tasas sin cambios el próximo mes, frente al 55% previo a la publicación de los datos del PCE, según cifras recientes de LSEG. * El rendimiento del bono a 30 años aumentó 5,42 puntos básicos al 5,6482%, tras haber cotizado al 5,6505%, su nivel más alto desde junio de 2002. El retorno a 2 años , que suele moverse en consonancia con las expectativas sobre las tasas de interés de la Fed, subió 0,21 puntos básicos al 4,891%, tras haber caído previamente al 4,8267%. * La curva que mide la diferencia entre las tasas a dos y 10 años , considerada un indicador de las expectativas económicas, se situó en 40,7 puntos básicos, tras haber alcanzado su mayor inclinación desde el 10 de septiembre. Sin embargo, desde finales de agosto, el diferencial se ha reducido casi 5 puntos básicos. * En septiembre, los retornos a 2 años registraban un avance de unos 53 puntos básicos, lo que supondría su mayor alza mensual desde febrero de 2023. La rentabilidad de referencia a 10 años también subían 53 puntos básicos, marcando su mayor ascenso mensual desde septiembre de 2022. * Los rendimientos a 30 años han aumentado unos 39 puntos básicos este mes, registrando su mayor incremento desde diciembre de 2024.

item.title: Monedas cierran mixtas tras dato inflación EEUU, acumulan baja mensual
item.description: Las principales monedas de América Latina registraron un cierre dispar el miércoles, en una jornada en la que el dólar cotizó estable, recuperándose luego de caer tras datos de la economía estadounidense que bajaron las expectativas de otra alza de tasas de interés de la Reserva Federal en octubre.
item.dc:creator: Froilan Romero
item.content:encoded: Las principales monedas de América Latina registraron un cierre dispar el miércoles, en una jornada en la que el dólar cotizó estable, recuperándose luego de caer tras datos de la economía estadounidense que bajaron las expectativas de otra alza de tasas de interés de la Reserva Federal en octubre. * Pero las divisas de la región anotaron marcadas pérdidas en septiembre, en un mes en que la Fed subió el costo del crédito en 25 puntos básicos y apuntó a que se podrían producir nuevos incrementos en su intento por frenar la inflación. Los mercados habían estado aumentando las apuestas por incrementos en octubre y diciembre. * [USN:L6N45M0TZ TEXT:"La inflación en Estados Unidos"] se aceleró menos de lo esperado en agosto. El índice de precios de los gastos de consumo personal (PCE) subió un 0,3% el mes pasado, tras un aumento revisado a la baja del 0,1% en julio, informó la Oficina de Análisis Económico del Departamento de Comercio (BEA, por su sigla en inglés). * Los contratos de futuros descontaban una probabilidad de apenas una entre tres de que se produjera una subida de tipos en octubre, aunque los operadores seguían anticipando un incremento para el mes de diciembre. * El índice dólar, que compara al billete verde con una cesta de seis destacadas monedas, cotizó estable, a 101,47 unidades. Aun así, acumuló alzas al cierre de septiembre, rompiendo una racha de dos meses consecutivos de pérdidas. * El peso mexicano cotizaba cerca del cierre en 18,0777 unidades por dólar, con una pérdida del 0,21%, para culminar septiembre con su mayor caída mensual en más de dos años, presionado por las expectativas de alzas de tasas por parte de la Fed y el diferencial de tipos con Banxico. * En el mes, la moneda acumulaba una pérdida del 5,7%, su peor desempeño desde agosto de 2024. * El principal índice accionario S&P/BMV IPC (.MXX) , que integran las 35 empresas más líquidas del mercado mexicano, bajaba un 1,44%, a 64.181,46 unidades. * El real brasileño se apreció un 0,76%, a 5,1735 unidades por dólar y subió un 0,15% en septiembre, mientras que el índice Bovespa (.BVSP) de la bolsa B3 de Sao Paulo escaló un 1,59%, a 186.752,25 puntos y acumuló un alza mensual de un 5,26%. * Los mercados brasileños tienen su atención puesta en las elecciones presidenciales del domingo. No se espera que haya un ganador y todo se definiría en un balotaje, donde el mandatario de izquierda Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva y el candidato de derecha Flávio Bolsonaro aparecen en un empate técnico, según las encuestas. * En Argentina, el peso mayorista se apreció un 0,2% a 1.519 por dólar . La moneda local interbancaria acumuló en el mes una caída del 0,66%. * La autoridad monetaria compró en septiembre por 473 millones de dólares, tras la adquisición de 160 millones con el cierre del mes y superar los 14.550 millones de dólares adquiridos en 2026. * En tanto, el índice bursátil Merval (.MERV) de la bolsa de Buenos Aires subía un 1,32%, ante compras de oportunidad, tras una racha de ocho sesiones negativas con un retroceso acumulado del 9,11%. * La plaza accionaria arrastró una pérdida del 7,07% durante septiembre bajo la nominación de pesos. * El peso chileno , bajó un 0,16%, a 974,50/974,80 por dólar y acumuló una caída del 4,16% en septiembre. En tanto, el principal índice de la bolsa de comercio de Santiago, el IPSA (.SPIPSA) , cedió un 0,78%, a 10.969,49 unidades. * La economía chilena presentó una serie de malas cifras económicas. El desempleo aumentó a 9,6% en el trimestre móvil a agosto, las manufacturas en Chile cayeron un 2,6% en el mismo mes y la producción de cobre, la mayor exportación del país, se hundió un 12,8% también en el octavo mes del año. * El peso colombiano cerró con alza de un 0,68% a 3.307,50 unidades por dólar, en su segunda sesión de ganancias, aunque en septiembre acumuló una depreciación del 2,88%. En tanto, el índice accionario MSCI COLCAP (.COLCAP) cedió un 0,38% a 2.549,13 puntos en la jornada. * [USN:L6N45M14N TEXT:"El Banco Central de Colombia"] incrementó el miércoles su tasa de interés de referencia en 25 puntos base a un 12,25%, una decisión que sorprendió a la mayoría del mercado en medio de las crecientes presiones inflacionarias, que amenazan con acentuarse por el eventual impacto del fenómeno climático de El Niño. * La moneda peruana, el sol subió un 0,23% en el día, a 3.4310/3.4330 unidades por dólar. Por otra parte, la Bolsa de Lima (.MXNUAMPESCPGPE) caía un 0,23%, a 1.584,31 puntos.

item.title: Texas US Senate candidate Paxton said Trump hurt Republicans, New York Times says
item.description: U.S. Senate candidate Ken Paxton told a group of donors that President Donald Trump's midterm convention hurt him and other Republicans running in November's elections, the New York Times reported on Wednesday, citing an audio recording of the candidate and attendees.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: U.S. Senate candidate Ken Paxton told a group of donors that President Donald Trump's midterm convention hurt him and other Republicans running in November's elections, the New York Times reported on Wednesday, citing an audio recording of the candidate and attendees. Paxton, who [USN:L6N41V0YO TEXT:"defeated"] four-term Senator John Cornyn in a Republican primary after receiving Trump's endorsement, made the remarks to a private gathering of conservative donors and lobbyists last Thursday, the Times reported. Reuters has not independently verified the recording. In the recording, someone asks Paxton, "Do you feel like he's a little bit of a drag?" the Times said. The questioner did not identify who he was asking about and that part of the recording was less distinct than Paxton's reply. "So to be honest with you, the numbers — when we did that convention — it dropped our numbers. Everybody’s numbers dropped. Right now, yeah, not good,” Paxton said in the audio clip posted on the newspaper's website. Trump on Wednesday told reporters he had not heard about the recording. "I can tell you that the convention was amazing," he said in the Oval Office. Paxton senior adviser Nick Maddux said in an emailed statement: "This is more manipulated nonsense from the New York Times to create a story that doesn’t exist." He added that Paxton is looking forward to Trump's [USN:L1N45L12S TEXT:"visit"] to Texas this week. The comments were made at a small private fundraiser in Washington, the Times reported. Three people with knowledge of the event confirmed Paxton's attendance; two of them remembered the question and one recalled Paxton's response, the report said. The audio recording was shared by an attendee who opposes Paxton's candidacy, it said. Trump gave Paxton his [USN:O8N40E01T TEXT:"blessing"] in the race against Cornyn in May and has praised the candidate since. Paxton faces Democratic state Representative James Talarico, a rising star and prodigious fundraiser, in the November election as Republicans seek to defend a narrow majority in the chamber. Independent polls have shown a tight race. Trump's MAGA Inc super PAC will spend at least $10 million on Paxton's campaign, according to a Federal Election Commission [USN:L1N44X04Z TEXT:"filing"] from early September. Trump and his Republican Party held the unusual [USN:L1N44V0PF TEXT:"convention"] in Dallas earlier in September, hoping to strengthen their midterm election prospects, but it does not appear to have had the desired effect. The president's popularity has declined since he launched a war on Iran in February that has disrupted oil shipments from the Middle East and pushed fuel prices near record highs, hitting US household finances. Since the war started, Trump's Republicans have also lost support, and in recent weeks have lost their longtime edge as the better party for economic policy. Last week, Trump's approval rating fell to 32% — lowest of his political career — as Republicans have soured on his handling of the cost of living amid the unpopular Iran war, a new [USN:L6N43U101 TEXT:"Reuters/Ipsos"] [USN:L6N45D0NV TEXT:"poll showed."]

item.title: Mercados financieros de Argentina cierran un septiembre complejo
item.description: La ronda de negocios financieros de Argentina cerró el miércoles un complejo septiembre con derrumbe de precios en activos y salto del riesgo país, en un contexto atravesado por crecientes dudas en la geopolítica global.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La ronda de negocios financieros de Argentina cerró el miércoles un complejo septiembre con derrumbe de precios en activos y salto del riesgo país, en un contexto atravesado por crecientes dudas en la geopolítica global. A los temores políticos internos se suman dudas externas ligadas al prolongado conflicto bélico en Oriente Medio que presiona sobre el petróleo y la inflación, más la perspectiva de una eventual nueva alza en la tasa de interés de Estados Unidos por parte de la Reserva Federal (Fed). Argentina irá a las urnas en 2027 para elegir presidente, contienda en la que el mandatario liberal Javier Milei dijo que buscará la reelección, aunque analistas proyectan que podría verse perjudicado por una eventual recesión en la economía. En medio de operaciones selectivas y con recorte de liquidez, el índice líder S&P Merval (.MERV) de la bolsa de Buenos Aires subió un 1,32% al cierre ante compras de oportunidad, tras una racha de ocho sesiones negativas con un acumulado del 9,11%. La plaza accionaria arrastró una pérdida del 7,07% durante septiembre bajo la nominación de pesos. La bolsa argentina "perforó los 1.800 puntos y en lo que va del mes bajó casi un 10% en dólares (...) Mientras tanto, la probabilidad de una suba de 25 puntos en la reunión de la Fed de octubre saltó del 54% al 75%", reportó Rava Bursátil. "Las reservas netas del banco central superan los 12.000 millones de dólares, pero descontando los desembolsos del FMI resultan negativas en unos 3.000 millones de dólares, mientras el riesgo país se acercó (recientemente) a 630 puntos básicos tras un salto desde los 485 de mediados de septiembre", agregó. El riesgo país argentino se ubicaba en los 607 puntos básicos (2000 GMT) de acuerdo al indicador elaborado a diario por el banco estadounidense J.P. Morgan, un nivel transitado la semana pasada y entre los más altos de los últimos seis meses. Por su parte, la comercialización de la deuda pública soberana arrojó un promedio diario positivo del 0,3%, en un mercado donde predomina la dolarización de carteras por las dudas inversoras reinantes. Este mercado de bonos acumuló una caída del 3,3% durante el noveno mes del 2026. "Terminamos un septiembre muy complejo, donde se multiplicaron las ventas de activos argentinos para tomar ganancias y cubrirse de las adversidades. Estamos en la etapa del 'miro y espero', por eso la retracción de liquidez que se evidencia", dijo un agente financiero del Banco Patagonia. El peso mayorista se apreció un tranquilo 0,2% a 1.519 por dólar , junto al BCRA que participa a diario con un rol de relevancia en los contratos a futuro para evitar fluctuaciones bruscas. La moneda local interbancaria acumuló en el mes una caída del 0,66%. La autoridad monetaria compró en septiembre por 473 millones de dólares, tras la adquisición de 160 millones con el cierre del mes y superar los 14.550 millones de dólares adquiridos en 2026.

item.title: S&P 500 cae y Nasdaq sube ante modesta alza de inflación
item.description: El Nasdaq subió el miércoles y el S&P 500 retrocedió, pero ambos anotaron su segunda ganancia trimestral consecutiva, ya que un dato de inflación más bajo de lo previsto enfrió las expectativas de que los responsables de la política monetaria de la Reserva Federal suban las tasas en octubre.
item.dc:creator: Chuck Mikolajczak, Shashwat Chauhan
item.content:encoded: El Nasdaq subió el miércoles y el S&P 500 retrocedió, pero ambos anotaron su segunda ganancia trimestral consecutiva, ya que un dato de inflación más bajo de lo previsto enfrió las expectativas de que los responsables de la política monetaria de la Reserva Federal suban las tasas en octubre. * Un informe del Departamento de Comercio reveló que el índice de precios del gasto en consumo personal (PCE) se situó en el 3,4% en términos interanuales en agosto, frente a las estimaciones de un 3,7% de los economistas encuestados por Reuters. * Por otra parte, los datos del PIB del segundo trimestre se revisaron al alza, para una tasa anualizada del 2,2%, gracias al robusto gasto de los consumidores y la inversión empresarial relacionada con la expansión de las infraestructuras de inteligencia artificial. * El aumento de los precios del crudo debido al conflicto entre Estados Unidos e Irán y los costos extremadamente altos del diésel han avivado la preocupación por la inflación y han impulsado los retornos de los bonos del Tesoro. Funcionarios de la Fed han indicado que podrían ser necesarias más alzas de tasas si las presiones sobre los precios no se moderan, luego de aumentar el costo del crédito en 25 puntos básicos este mes. * Las expectativas del mercado de una subida de tasas de al menos 25 puntos básicos en la reunión de octubre de la Fed cayeron a cerca del 39%, según la herramienta FedWatch de CME, frente al 51% de la sesión anterior y al 71% de hace una semana. * Según datos preliminares, el S&P 500 (.SPX) perdió 18,13 puntos, o un 0,23%, a 7.652,71 unidades; el Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) ganó 66,46 puntos, o un 0,25%, a 26.864 unidades; y el Promedio Industrial Dow Jones (.DJI) cayó 431,84 puntos, o un 0,84%, a 50.918,08 unidades. * Tanto el S&P 500 como el Nasdaq registraron sus segundos avances trimestrales consecutivos y el quinto en los últimos seis trimestres. El Dow experimentó un descenso trimestral por segunda vez en tres trimestres. * La mayoría de las acciones de gran capitalización y de crecimiento registraron ligeras alzas; Amazon.com (AMZN.O) , Apple (AAPL.O) y Nvidia (NVDA.O) avanzaron, impulsando a su vez al índice tecnológico del S&P 500 (.SPLRCT) , que fue el sector con mejor desempeño en la jornada.

item.title: Experimental Lilly combination drug tops Zepbound in weight-loss trial
item.description: Eli Lilly said on Wednesday its experimental combination weight-loss drug outperformed its blockbuster Zepbound in a head-to-head trial, intensifying the competition with Danish rival Novo Nordisk for new, more effective obesity therapies.
item.dc:creator: Patrick Wingrove
item.content:encoded: Eli Lilly (LLY.N) said on Wednesday its experimental combination weight-loss drug outperformed its blockbuster Zepbound in a head-to-head trial, intensifying the competition with Danish rival Novo Nordisk (NOVOb.CO) for new, more effective obesity therapies. The Indianapolis-based drugmaker said patients with diabetes on the highest tested dose of EloraTZP, which combines tirzepatide and experimental drug eloralintide, lost an average of 23.3% of body weight over 48 weeks. That compared with 14.8% for patients on the highest dose of Zepbound in the mid-stage trial. Tirzepatide is the active ingredient in Zepbound as well as Lilly's diabetes drug Mounjaro. Kenneth Custer, president of Lilly's cardiometabolic health division, said in an interview that he expected the combo drug would offer "the best balance of efficacy, safety, and tolerability" within Lilly's obesity portfolio and among competitors. "The findings provide strong combination proof-of-concept and broaden Lilly's cardiometabolic portfolio beyond today's incretin standards," Citi analyst Geoff Meacham said. Achieving tirzepatide-like weight loss in patients with type 2 diabetes was significant, as diabetes typically tempers treatment efficacy, he added. Custer said it was possible the combination could lead to even greater weight loss in later trials than retatrutide, another promising Lilly experimental obesity medication. In [USN:L1N41X0TA TEXT:"a late-stage trial"], the highest dose of retatrutide drove an average weight reduction of up to 28.3% over 80 weeks in patients without diabetes. EloraTZP also cut blood sugar levels, lowering A1C by up to 2.9% versus 2.4% for tirzepatide alone, according to data presented at the European Association for the Study of Diabetes meeting in Milan. Lilly shares fell marginally despite strong efficacy data, as investors focused on adherence and long-term persistence. "The outsized weight loss benefit is being questioned relative to the discontinuation rates and the reality that this is a dual-drug regime," said Kevin Gade, COO at Bahl & Gaynor, which holds Lilly shares. Patients stopped taking EloraTZP in the trial at a rate of 10.8% to 27%, depending on the severity of side effects as multiple doses were tested. That compared with a dropout rate of 0% to 10.8% with eloralintide alone, 2.9% for tirzepatide and 16.7% for those who received a placebo. The most common side effects were mild to moderate gastrointestinal issues that occurred mainly during dose escalation and were more frequent in the combination arms than with either drug alone, the company said. "If Lilly can get a handle on the discontinuations and GI tolerability issues, then I think this is looking stronger than retatrutide as a high-efficacy option for patients," said Morningstar analyst Karen Andersen. Lilly, in a press conference to discuss the results, said the higher discontinuation rate was due to patients ramping up doses of two drugs at once. It said the company would improve escalation schedules in longer, late-stage trials. COMPETITIVE LANDSCAPE The results raise the stakes in a fight between Lilly and Novo for share of the global weight-loss market forecast by some analysts to reach $100 billion to $150 billion annually by the end of the decade. Novo is on track to launch the first combination obesity drug, CagriSema, early next year. Expectations for that medication took a hit in February when it fell short of Lilly's high-dose tirzepatide in a head-to-head trial, despite achieving a 23% average weight reduction over 84 weeks. Novo's long-term growth prospects continue to rest on pipeline programs beyond CagriSema, led by its next-generation dual-acting tablet zenagamtide, Morningstar's Andersen said. The company's fortunes have reversed sharply from its days of dominating the market with the 2021 arrival of its powerful obesity drug Wegovy that propelled its valuation above $600 billion. The Danish drugmaker's shares have tumbled more than 70% from their record highs in the face of stiff competition from US rival Lilly. Eli Lilly executives said it was too early to determine the ideal patient profile for its combination therapy. But they noted that it could serve individuals needing 20% to 30% weight loss, or those who fail to achieve their goals on Zepbound, by targeting a hormone pathway linked to hunger and thoughts about food. Eloralintide belongs to a class of drugs known as selective amylin receptor agonists, which target a different hormone than GLP-1 drug Zepbound. In the multi-arm EloraTZP trial of 367 obese or overweight adults with type 2 diabetes in the US and Argentina, eloralintide alone led to an average weight loss of 12.3% on the second highest dose tested, and 11.1% on the highest, while those taking a placebo lost just 3%. The company said it plans to start late-stage trials for EloraTZP in the fourth quarter of 2026, while late-stage trials of eloralintide in obese and overweight patients with and without diabetes were ongoing.

item.title: Passengers foil bid to crash Dubai-Tel Aviv flight, Israel says, after co-pilot-on-pilot stabbing
item.description: Passengers and crew entered the cockpit, overpowered the co-pilot and enabled a second pair of flydubai pilots aboard the flight to land the jet safely in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia, Israeli officials said.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Cornwell, Federico Maccioni, Pesha Magid
item.content:encoded: Passengers on a flydubai flight reached Israel safely on Wednesday after customers and crew foiled a co-pilot's attempt to crash the aircraft, Israeli officials said, in a struggle that began when he stabbed the pilot and sent the jet plunging nearly 14,000 feet in less than 30 seconds. Passengers and crew entered the cockpit, overpowered the co-pilot and enabled a second pair of flydubai pilots who were aboard the flight to land the jet safely in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia, Israeli officials said. More than 10 hours later, the passengers arrived at Tel Aviv's Ben Gurion Airport aboard a flydubai replacement aircraft, with several describing the episode as a miracle and recounting a frantic struggle to prevent a catastrophe. Israeli officials said the attacker's motive aboard flight FZ1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv remained under investigation. Israel and the United Arab Emirates, which includes Dubai, signed the Abraham Accords normalizing relations in 2020. The incident sharpened concerns about global aviation security in a region scarred by years of conflict, prompting Israel to tighten checks on pilots flying into the country. "I just can say that it was a miracle. It was awful, crazy, and we thank God that we survived it, we didn't think we will make it but thank God we are in Israel. We are back home. And we are happy to see everyone here," passenger Lital Shachaf said. Israel's ambulance service said a 51-year-old man was taken to an Israeli hospital to be treated for injuries to his upper body. The man was in a "mild condition," it said. Describing the event as "a serious security incident," Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Saudi authorities would interrogate the co-pilot. Flydubai said in a statement that the underlying reasons for the event remained unknown and warned against "premature speculation." An Israeli official identified the co-pilot as an Omani national. There was no immediate comment from Oman. Israeli officials applauded the passengers, who they credited with avoiding a much more serious disaster. Netanyahu said there were 174 people on board the flight from Dubai, most of them Israeli nationals. 'SOMETHING YOU DO WITHOUT THINKING' A Netanyahu spokesperson told Reuters that the wounded captain, identified by the Israeli leader's office as Smit Machchhar, an Indian national, was covered with blood on the floor when he managed to click the release to open the cockpit door. Passengers who entered found the co-pilot bashing at the plane's control panel, the spokesperson said.“This is something you do without thinking, just running to save your daughter’s life, your family’s life,” said Asaf Rajuan, one of the passengers who helped restrain the attacker. He spoke with a forehead still bloodied from the struggle. Netanyahu's office released a video showing the prime minister at Ben Gurion Airport giving a hug to another passenger, Yaniv Hayun, who his office said "broke into" the cockpit. "I see you and I see a lion – a big hero," Netanyahu told the man, who was still wearing the blood-stained shirt he had on during the flight. Flydubai operates daily return flights between Dubai and Tel Aviv, a route that is popular among Israeli nationals. The flight path normally uses airspace over Saudi Arabia and Jordan. It is not the first time a flight between Israel and the UAE has landed in Saudi Arabia. A flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv made an emergency landing in Riyadh in September 2025 due to a medical incident, Israeli media reported at the time. Saudi Arabia's Tabuk airport, where the plane landed, said both pilots had been hospitalised after sustaining injuries. The incident heightened security fears in Israel weeks before Israelis vote in the first election since the Hamas-led October 7, 2023, attacks, with Israel's security figuring prominently in the campaigning. Responding to the incident on X, far-right security minister Itamar Ben-Gvir wrote, "Terrorism is a devil with whom no agreement must be reached". ISRAEL TO TIGHTEN CHECKS ON PILOTS FLYING TO ISRAEL Israeli media published conflicting reports on the incident, with some outlets reporting that a pilot had tried to crash the passenger plane in an alleged suicide attempt. Some Israeli media outlets initially identified the pilots as Omani and Emirati nationals, while others said they were Russian and Ukrainian. "Every pilot that is going to be flying into Israel, we are going to know the pilots' identities, know who they are, and do some type of security check," Doron Spielman, a Netanyahu spokesperson, told Reuters. Netanyahu met on Sunday with UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan during a rare visit to the Gulf country. Israel and the UAE have forged close security, military and economic ties since establishing diplomatic ties. Israel provided the UAE earlier this year with Iron Dome air-defence systems and Israeli personnel to operate them, helping defend against Iranian attacks launched after Israel and the US began strikes on Iran. The UAE government had yet to comment on the flydubai incident, while the Dubai state-owned airline said an "altercation" occurred in the cockpit and the flight subsequently diverted to Tabuk, where it landed safely. The UAE's aviation regulator, the GCAA, said the flight "experienced a security incident that was brought under control".

item.title: Banco Central de Colombia sorprende con incremento de su tasa de interés
item.description: El Banco Central de Colombia incrementó el miércoles su tasa de interés de referencia en 25 puntos base, a 12,25%, una decisión que sorprendió a la mayoría del mercado en medio de las crecientes presiones inflacionarias, que amenazan con acentuarse por el eventual impacto del fenómeno climático de El Niño.
item.dc:creator: Nelson Bocanegra, Carlos Vargas
item.content:encoded: El Banco Central de Colombia incrementó el miércoles su tasa de interés de referencia en 25 puntos base, a 12,25%, una decisión que sorprendió a la mayoría del mercado en medio de las crecientes presiones inflacionarias, que amenazan con acentuarse por el eventual impacto del fenómeno climático de El Niño. En un reciente sondeo de Reuters, 19 de los 27 analistas anticiparon que la autoridad monetaria mantendría estable la tasa en el 12%, mientras que seis proyectaron un aumento de 50 puntos base y los dos restantes pronosticaron un alza de 25 puntos base. La decisión contó con el voto de cuatro de los siete miembros del directorio de la autoridad monetaria. Dos se inclinaron por dejarla estable y uno por aumentarla en 50 puntos base. El ministro de Hacienda, Miguel Gómez, dijo que votó por el incremento de 25 puntos base. Con el ajuste, la tasa alcanzó uno de los niveles más altos desde febrero de 2024, cuando se situó en 12,75%. "La materialización del Fenómeno de El Niño podría continuar presionando al alza las sendas de alimentos y regulados", dijo el gerente del banco, Leonardo Villar, al leer un comunicado. "La decisión adoptada por la Junta Directiva mantiene una política monetaria restrictiva, consistente con la perspectiva de una senda de inflación decreciente en 2027", explicó. La inflación en Colombia alcanzó al cierre de agosto un 6,24% anual, más del doble de la meta del Banco Central de 3% y amenaza con seguir subiendo por el eventual impacto de El Niño sobre los precios. "Al Gobierno le preocupa mucho la persistencia del fenómeno inflacionario porque la inflación es un impuesto que castiga particularmente a las personas más pobres", explicó el ministro Gómez, quien participó en su primera reunión de política monetaria en representación del Gobierno. El funcionario aseguró que al fenómeno climático se sumó el eventual impacto del terremoto que sufrió el país en agosto, así como el incremento de la tasa de interés en Estados Unidos. Una amplia región del suroeste y del centro de Colombia fue sacudida el 10 de agosto por un terremoto de magnitud 7,4 que dejó 335 muertos y miles de heridos, destruyó casas, edificios e infraestructura. El incremento de la tasa se produjo después de que el Banco Central mantuvo estable el costo referencial del dinero en la reunión de julio, tras los incrementos de enero, marzo y junio pasados. En agosto no hubo reunión de política monetaria. La reunión del Banco Central colombiano se realizó luego de que este mes la Reserva Federal de Estados Unidos subió sus tasas de interés, mientras que el Reino Unido y México las mantuvieron estables y Brasil las redujo.

item.title: Protesters camped out across Spain demand passage of housing measures
item.description: Thousands of protesters camped out on Madrid's main square and in other Spanish cities demanded on Wednesday that parliament swiftly approve new measures to protect tenants and curb the country's acute housing crisis.
item.dc:creator: David Latona, Guillermo Martinez
item.content:encoded: Thousands of protesters camped out on Madrid's main square and in other Spanish cities demanded on Wednesday that parliament swiftly approve new measures to protect tenants and curb the country's acute housing crisis. The demonstrations were ignited last week by the [USN:L8N45F0PQ TEXT:"dramatic eviction"] of an 87-year-old woman from her Madrid home of more than seven decades. Her case highlighted mounting pressure on long-term tenants in major cities and tourist hotspots, where soaring rents, gentrification and a shortage of affordable housing have fuelled social and political unrest. Spain's leftist minority government [USN:L1N45L0A6 TEXT:"passed two decrees"] on Tuesday with a host of measures, including a ban on evictions of vulnerable tenants until 2030, but their full implementation hinges on approval by the fragmented lower house, which is due to hold a vote on Friday. Many activists said even those measures fell short of tackling the crisis. "It's not enough — it might be a starting point or a stopgap," 32-year-old pharmaceutical worker Julio Gomez told Reuters, adding that he was willing to stay with his tent in Madrid's Puerta del Sol square for "as long as it takes". Others criticised the government's decision to split the measures into two separate bills with the expectation that one, which automatically extends leases to prevent abusive rent hikes, would be rejected by a slim right-wing majority. "They've done it so that one gets approved and the stronger one gets rejected, just to sneak one through by the skin of its teeth," said veterinarian Gonzalo Sanchez, 26. ACTIVISTS FIGHT EVICTIONS Madrid's Tenants' Union, which organised the initial protests, described some of the measures as "crumbs", although it also called the government's move a "historic victory" for the social movement. Meanwhile, dozens gathered on Wednesday in Burjassot, near Valencia, to block the eviction of Daniel Gonzalez, a university professor who has lived at his home since 2009. Faced with the protest, court officials agreed to postpone his eviction for at least 10 days. Gonzalez said he has paid rent on time for more than 17 years, despite the property changing hands among investment funds, but after a legal dispute lasting nearly a decade the courts ultimately backed the owner. The public outcry over last week's eviction of 87-year-old Maricarmen Abascal in Madrid led to a deal with her landlord, property firm Urbagestion, to let her stay in the apartment with unchanged rent. She remains in hospital following the eviction but is expected to return home in the coming days. Urbagestion's co-owner, Ricardo Alonso, told newspaper El Economista he and his partner had faced a pressure campaign over the eviction, citing the delivery of a box containing live cockroaches.

item.title: Turkey orders detention of 34 more suspects in widening investment fund probe
item.description: Turkish authorities ordered the detention of 34 more suspects as part of an investigation into alleged market manipulation and funds, Justice Minister Akin Gurlek said on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Turkish authorities ordered the detention of 34 more suspects as part of an investigation into alleged market manipulation and funds, Justice Minister Akin Gurlek said on Wednesday. In a post on X, Gurlek said authorities were also examining trading activity in 26 stocks listed on Borsa Istanbul deemed to have been subject to manipulative transactions, money transfers and connections to individuals and accounts that generated unusually large gains. He added that legal procedures would be launched to transfer assets determined to be proceeds of crime to a fund established under the Savings Deposit Insurance Fund (TMSF). Turkey's [USN:L6N45L0PJ TEXT:"fund crisis"] erupted after suspected price manipulation in a number of thinly traded stocks triggered heavy losses and redemption pressures at investment funds. Almost half a million investors hold stakes in more than 100 Turkish investment funds with combined assets of $20 billion that authorities ordered to be [USN:L6N45L147 TEXT:"liquidated"] this month. Gurlek said the latest operation brings the total number of suspects targeted in the probe to 217, including 56 jailed pending trial and 88 placed under judicial supervision while the investigation continues.

item.title: Paramount names Mattel boss Kreiz as co-CEO
item.description: Paramount Skydance named Mattel CEO Ynon Kreiz, who led the toymaker's transformation into a broader entertainment company, as the co-CEO of the combined firm following its $110 billion Warner Bros deal.
item.dc:creator: Neil Kanatt
item.content:encoded: Paramount Skydance (PSKY.O) named Mattel (MAT.O) CEO Ynon Kreiz, who led the toymaker's transformation into a broader entertainment company, as the co-CEO of the combined firm following its $110 billion Warner Bros [USN:L6N45D0SG TEXT:"deal"]. The change comes ahead of the crucial holiday season, with Mattel facing tariff-related costs and activist investor pressure over its declining shareholder value despite efforts to build on the success of 2023's blockbuster "Barbie" movie. Mattel's board member Roger Lynch, who was the head of Vogue and the New Yorker owner Condé Nast, will take over the helm from Kreiz, the company said in a separate statement on Wednesday. Kreiz will be starting his new position at Paramount as the co-CEO effective October 5 and will also join its board, Paramount said. Kreiz's push to turn Mattel's intellectual property into films, television shows and digital games delivered the global box-office hit "Barbie" and boosted demand for its merchandise. Yet Mattel shares have risen just 5% during Kreiz's tenure as CEO, sharply underperforming a nearly 200% gain in the S&P 500 (.SPX) over the same period. "This announcement adds a layer of uncertainty to an already skittish investor sentiment given a tougher macro backdrop, rising rates, and likely a more Q4-weighted outcome," UBS analysts wrote in a note. Earlier this year, investor Southeastern Asset Management urged [USN:L4N41L1BU TEXT:"Mattel to explore options"], including a sale of the company or a combination with rival Hasbro (HAS.O) . Lynch has served on Mattel's board since 2018 and is expected to assume the top role by November 2. Meanwhile, Condé Nast, where Lynch has been CEO for about seven years, named board member Mike Perlis as interim CEO. Lynch, who will be taking the helm of a sixth company, is best known for leading Condé Nast, Pandora and Sling TV, bringing media, satellite and digital expertise but little direct experience in the toy industry. "Roger's appointment comes at a time when the lines between consumer products and media are more blurred than ever, so it makes sense to place an experienced media operator at the helm," said James Zahn, editor-in-chief at The Toy Book. Last month, Mattel [USN:L6N4411GM TEXT:"topped"] second-quarter revenue estimates and reaffirmed its annual targets, but tariff-related costs and investments to boost sales resulted in profit missing market expectations.

item.title: Dólar cotiza estable frente a sus pares tras datos de inflación EEUU menores a lo esperado
item.description: El dólar cotizó estable frente a las principales divisas el miércoles, tras conocerse datos que mostraron una aceleración de la inflación en Estados Unidos menor de lo previsto, lo que redujo las apuestas del mercado a un alza de las tasas de interés por parte de la Reserva Federal.
item.dc:creator: Chibuike Oguh
item.content:encoded: El dólar cotizó estable frente a las principales divisas el miércoles, tras conocerse datos que mostraron una aceleración de la inflación en Estados Unidos menor de lo previsto, lo que redujo las apuestas del mercado a un alza de las tasas de interés por parte de la Reserva Federal. * El dólar se había estado fortaleciendo a la par del alza en el rendimiento de los bonos del Tesoro estadounidense, impulsado por las crecientes expectativas de nuevas subidas de tasas de la Fed en un contexto de inflación alimentada por el aumento de los precios del petróleo. El billete verde anotó alzas mensuales contra el euro, el franco suizo y la libra esterlina. * Sin embargo, el dólar recortó parte de aquellas ganancias tras los datos, antes de recuperarse, mientras que el retorno de las notas caía en todos sus vencimientos. El de la deuda a dos años, que suele moverse en línea con las expectativas de tasas de la Fed, bajó 0,4 puntos básicos, al 4,885%. * El euro cotizó estable, a 1,1330 dólares, y marcó una pérdida mensual tras dos meses consecutivos de ganancias. * Los datos del Departamento de Comercio mostraron que el índice de precios de los gastos de consumo personal, el indicador de inflación preferido de la Fed, aumentó un 0,3% el mes pasado. Los economistas encuestados por Reuters esperaban un incremento del 0,4%. * Los operadores ahora valoran una probabilidad del 37% de un alza de tasas por parte de la Fed en octubre, muy por debajo del 70% de hace una semana, según la herramienta FedWatch de CME. * La moneda estadounidense también se negoció casi sin cambios frente al yen, a 157,34 unidades por dólar. Ganó un 0,26% ante el franco suizo y marcó su segundo mes seguido de avance. * La libra esterlina , en tanto, se fortaleció un 0,26%, a 1,3265 dólares, pero en el mes descendió tras dos alzas mensuales consecutivas. * El índice dólar, que compara al billete verde con una cesta de seis destacadas monedas, cotizó estable, a 101,47 unidades. Aun así, acumuló alzas al cierre de septiembre, rompiendo una racha de dos meses consecutivos de pérdidas.

item.title: TSX edges lower as miners weigh; investors assess US inflation data, falls for month
item.description: Canada's main stock index edged lower on Wednesday to end down for the month as declines in mining and other sectors outweighed gains in energy stocks, while investors assessed softer-than-expected US inflation data.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Canada's main stock index edged lower on Wednesday to end down for the month as declines in mining and other sectors outweighed gains in energy stocks, while investors assessed softer-than-expected US inflation data. The Toronto Stock Exchange's S&P/TSX Composite Index (.GSPTSE) fell 0.63% to 35,235.87 points at the close. Trade was relatively quiet for an end-of-month session on the TSX due to Canada's National Day for Truth and Reconciliation, a holiday recognized by many companies, institutions and governments. The TSX notched a loss for the month, falling 2.9% from 36,270 on August 31 to 35,235 on September 30. The Canadian benchmark snapped a five-month winning streak following a volatile September marked by rising global bond yields, a Fed rate hike and escalating Canada-US trade tensions. US stock indexes moved higher as [USN:L4N45M0V5 TEXT:"cooler-than-expected"] inflation data reduced expectations that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates again next month On the TSX, sectors were split between gainers and losers. Mining shares dropped 1% as gold and silver fell Ag Growth International (AFN.TO) soared almost 28% on the company saying it had achieved covenant relief on its financing The healthcare sector was the biggest decliner, down more than 2%, with medical cannabis producer Curaleaf Holdings (CURA.TO) falling over 7%. Materials and financials also fell. The energy sector (.SPTTEN) and Telecoms led gains. Brent crude was on track for a monthly gain of about 14%, its biggest since July, as US-Iran talks aimed at ending their war stalled and tight fuel markets continued to underpin prices. "It's going to be really volatile day-to-day. There's no clear directional move until we get more stability and clarity out of the Middle East," said Michael Dehal, senior portfolio manager at Dehal Investment Partners at Raymond James Still, the index was on track to post a ninth straight quarterly gain, its longest such streak on record. Among other movers, First Quantum Minerals (FM.TO) initially slumped 31% after Panama's government recommended an [USN:S0N3ST09K TEXT:"orderly closure"] of the mining company's Cobre Panama mine, but regained about half the losses during the session.

item.title: Crudo sube cerca de 1 dólar por la falta de avances entre EEUU e Irán
item.description: Los precios del crudo subieron alrededor de 1 dólar el miércoles y acabaron septiembre con un fuerte alza mensual, debido al estancamiento de las negociaciones entre Estados Unidos e Irán y la escasez en los mercados de combustible.
item.dc:creator: Laila Kearney
item.content:encoded: Los precios del crudo subieron alrededor de 1 dólar el miércoles y acabaron septiembre con un fuerte alza mensual, debido al estancamiento de las negociaciones entre Estados Unidos e Irán y la escasez en los mercados de combustible. Los futuros del Brent para noviembre , que vencen este miércoles, cerraron con un alza de 91 centavos, o un 0,9%, a 103,5 dólares el barril. El contrato más activo, el de diciembre , ganó 1,87 dólares, o un 1,9%, a 97,1 dólares. El West Texas Intermediate en Estados Unidos (WTI) avanzó 1,4 dólares, o un 1,2%, a 90,42 dólares. El Brent subió 14% en el mes, mientras que el WTI aumentó aproximadamente un 4%. Qatar dijo el martes que espera que la diplomacia itinerante entre Teherán y Washington pueda dar lugar a un avance decisivo. Sin embargo, el presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, desmintió informaciones de Axios y CNN, que citaron a funcionarios estadounidenses, que habían dicho que Washington está dispuesto a aliviar las sanciones a Irán y a desbloquear los fondos congelados a cambio de medidas "concretas" en relación con su programa nuclear. El martes, Arabia Saudita reanudó las cargas de petroleros desde su puerto de Yanbu, en el mar Rojo, tras reanudar las operaciones en su oleoducto Este-Oeste. Goldman Sachs estima que las exportaciones de petróleo del Golfo se han recuperado hasta alcanzar los 23,3 millones de barriles al día durante la última semana, en línea con su promedio para 2025, ya que las exportaciones se duplicaron en septiembre, según una nota del martes. En los últimos cinco días, el promedio de diez días de las exportaciones totales de petróleo se ha mantenido en 20,5 millones de barriles al día, lo que supone el 89% de los niveles de 2025, según estimaciones de JPMorgan.

item.title: Antin to sell majority of US-based Vicinity Energy to Harrison Street
item.description: Antin Infrastructure has agreed to sell a majority stake in US-based Vicinity Energy to Harrison Street, the French private equity firm said on Wednesday, sending its shares 3.7% higher by 1053 GMT.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Antin Infrastructure (ANTIN.PA) has agreed to sell a majority stake in US-based Vicinity Energy to Harrison Street, the French private equity firm said on Wednesday, sending its shares 3.7% higher by 1053 GMT. The deal gives Vicinity an enterprise value of $2.92 billion and is expected to close in the first half of 2027, pending regulatory approvals. Harrison Street plans to buy the stake through a joint venture with Kenon Holdings (KEN.N) Antin created Vicinity in 2019 through the carve-out of Veolia's (VIE.PA) US district energy business Vicinity provides district heating and cooling services to over 1,000 buildings across 12 major US cities under long-term contracts
